input.rationale: Filed a successor of the live-cluster experiment that adds the healing phase, because the current account still lists the post-healing fate of the conflicting entry and the long-run persistence of the stale membership as unobserved. The scenario, admissions, identity fields and the seven existing comparisons are carried over unchanged; the harness now reconnects the full mesh after the split, waits for one leader, applies one more entry and samples the log entry both leaders committed at (index 11, term 3) on all five nodes plus the restarted node's configuration. Local construction feedback is deterministic on those three additions across four runs (entry payloads A:minority-write, C:minority-write against B,D,E:majority-write all at term 3 so the entries cannot be reconciled by term comparison; the restarted node's configuration still {A,B,C} while its log advances to 12; the cluster keeps committing). The healed leader's identity did vary between runs (A once, D or E three times), so no comparison asserts on it; those operands are recorded but not asserted.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} long enough for both sides to elect and commit, and is then healed while sampling the conflicting index and the restarted node's configuration.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations only: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter(D), AddVoter(E) and one further apply.

A is shut down gracefully and restarted from its own store objects; all five nodes run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the persisted commit index the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
The partition and the healing are expressed only by transport disconnection and reconnection in both directions; timings, RPC lifecycles and election rules are untouched.
The healing sample is taken after the sole leader has committed one further entry plus 300 ms; no assertion depends on which node won that election.
excluded: No crash, storage fault or snapshot installation is exercised; the scenario ends with the healed sample.
The fate of the conflicting entry beyond the sampled window (for example after a snapshot install or log compaction) is not observed.
No repository test was executed.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. It starts D and E, adds each as voter through the leader, applies one further command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry, and emits 'fixture' with the snapshot index and membership, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores with the feature on and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome' with leaders, terms, leader count, per-node leader booleans, reported configurations, write errors, write indexes and terms, payloads and the derived conflicting_commits. It then reconnects the full mesh, waits for exactly one leader, applies one further entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' with each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, payload consistency, same_term_conflicting_payload, per-node log last indexes, the restarted node's configuration, B's configuration, the leader's configuration and log index, the number of nodes behind the leader and post_heal_apply_error; all nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed.
semantic_changes: After the outcome sample the harness reconnects every transport pair, waits up to 15s for exactly one leader, applies one further entry on that leader and waits 300ms.

A fourth event 'healed' reports each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, whether those payloads are consistent, whether they conflict at equal terms, each node's log last index, the restarted node's configuration and each side's reported configuration, plus derived operands a_log_advanced_after_heal and nodes_with_log_behind_leader.

Three comparisons are added on the 'healed' event: entry payloads at the conflicting index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership after the cluster runs on, and its log must have advanced.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft configuration scan plus the RestoreCommittedLogs replay; the AppendEntries log-matching rule (truncate only on term difference, skip same-term duplicates) is responsible for whether the divergent entries can be reconciled.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration while both sides lead.
After the partition heals, all nodes must hold the same entry at the index both leaders committed at.
Once the cluster is whole again and committing new entries, the restarted node must use the committed membership.
Progress control: the restarted node's log did advance after healing, so the stale membership is not a stalled state.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a healing phase after the split-brain window and three comparisons over it; the fixture, restart, partition, admissions and the seven earlier comparisons are unchanged.

scope.description: Restart-shaped construction of a single node (LocalID A, ProtocolVersion 3, in-memory log/stable/snapshot stores) whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, observed with RestoreCommittedLogs off, on (construction only), and on with background goroutines started.
assumptions: The stores, configuration contents and their indexes are supplied by the harness: snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1, log entries 1..7 with a LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, and a persisted commit index of 7 (StageCommitIndex), which is a state a follower can reach after committing a configuration change and crashing before taking a newer snapshot.
The FSM discards applied entries and its Restore accepts the snapshot bytes; snapshot restore therefore succeeds and lastApplied after restore is the snapshot index.
For the two construction cases conf.skipStartup is true, so no background goroutine runs and r.configurations is read directly as the state NewRaft computed.

For the live case the node runs normally (default timeouts) with no reachable peers, and the sample is taken only after the node has entered the candidate loop; the public GetConfiguration copy is read instead of r.configurations.
excluded: The election/quorum consequence is not executed here: no election with a majority of the current configuration and a minority of a stale one is run.
The snapshot was produced by the harness rather than by a live Snapshot() call, so the fixture's log/snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: For each mode the harness creates a fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it writes a version-1 snapshot at index 5, term 1 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; it stores log entries 1=LogConfiguration{A,B,C}, 2..5=LogNoop, 6=LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, 7=LogNoop; it calls logs.StageCommitIndex(7). It then emits a 'fixture' event describing those stored facts, builds Config with DefaultConfig(), LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, fsm, logs, stable, snaps, trans). In the two construction modes conf.skipStartup is left true, and a 'construct' event reports lastApplied, commit index, latest/committed configuration id sets and indexes, quorumSize, hasVote(self), the number of batches queued on fsmMutateCh and the number of FSM restores. In the live mode the background goroutines run; a 'live' event reports the public GetConfiguration id set, the node state and current term. Modes run in the order baseline, restore_committed, restore_committed_skip_startup_false so the emitted event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, live.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft startup path: NewRaft's configuration scan (api.go) combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay (api.go restoreFromCommittedLogs -> raft.go processLogs); the node is responsible for using the configuration of the latest configuration entry in its own log.

comparisons.description: Feature on: the constructed node's latest configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry at index 6 in its own log.
Feature off control on the identical stores: the same assertion about latest configuration.
Feature on: the node's election quorum should be the majority of the five voters recorded by the committed configuration entry.
Feature off control: quorum from the same log.
Mechanism operand: with the feature on, the replay advanced lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the configuration scan.
Mechanism operand control: without the replay lastApplied is the snapshot index, so the scan covers index 6.
Running node with the feature on: the configuration reported through the public GetConfiguration should be the committed membership, sampled while the node is campaigning.

knowledge.assertion: scan start index is max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1
restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) before the scan, advancing lastApplied

semantic_changes: CA_EVENT objects now carry a string 'event' field naming the event (fixture/construct/live) instead of an 'alias' field, so the runner can parse them into observations.
The emitted field sets, event order, modes, store fixtures and comparison definitions are otherwise identical to the previous experiment.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: the restarted node is responsible for deriving candidate admission and election quorum from the latest configuration entry in its own log, and voters are responsible for granting at most the votes their own view of the configuration requires.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log; this is the same predicate the earlier supplied-fixture experiment declared, here with stores produced by real operations.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader; both partitions observed here are disjoint halves of one cluster.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration, so the two sides disagree about membership while both lead.

knowledge.assertion: the persisted commit index exists only when the node ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled

Three comparisons were added: entry payloads at that index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership once the cluster is whole and committing, and its log must have advanced as a progress control. scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: the restarted node is responsible for deriving candidate admission and election quorum from the latest configuration entry in its own log, and voters are responsible for granting at most the votes their own view of the configuration requires.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log; this is the same predicate the earlier supplied-fixture experiment declared, here with stores produced by real operations.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader; both partitions observed here are disjoint halves of one cluster.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.
The rest of the cluster still reports the current five-voter configuration, so the two sides disagree about membership while both lead.

knowledge.assertion: the persisted commit index exists only when the node ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled

semantic_changes: After the outcome sample the harness reconnects every transport pair, waits up to 15s for exactly one leader, applies one further entry on that leader and waits 300ms.

A fourth event 'healed' reports each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, whether those payloads are consistent, whether they conflict at equal terms, each node's log last index, the restarted node's configuration and each side's reported configuration, plus derived operands a_log_advanced_after_heal and nodes_with_log_behind_leader.

Three comparisons are added on the 'healed' event: entry payloads at the conflicting index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership after the cluster runs on, and its log must have advanced.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} long enough for both sides to elect and commit, and is then healed while sampling the conflicting index and the restarted node's configuration.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations only: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, committed applies, a user snapshot on A, AddVoter(D), AddVoter(E) and one further apply.

A is shut down gracefully and restarted from its own store objects; all five nodes run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the persisted commit index the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.

The healing sample is taken after the sole leader has committed one further entry plus 300 ms; no assertion depends on which node won that election.
excluded: No crash, storage fault or snapshot installation is exercised; the scenario ends with the healed sample.
The fate of the conflicting entry beyond the sampled window (for example after a snapshot install or log compaction) is not observed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. It starts D and E, adds each as voter through the leader, applies one further command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry, and emits 'fixture' with the snapshot index and membership, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A from the same stores with the feature on and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader in each partition, submits one Apply to each leader, reads both leaders' entries at the shared index and emits 'outcome' with leaders, terms, leader count, per-node leader booleans, reported configurations, write errors, write indexes and terms, payloads and the derived conflicting_commits. It then reconnects the full mesh, waits for exactly one leader, applies one further entry, waits 300ms and emits 'healed' with each node's payload and term at the conflicting index, payload consistency, same_term_conflicting_payload, per-node log last indexes, the restarted node's configuration, B's configuration, the leader's configuration and log index, the number of nodes behind the leader and post_heal_apply_error; all nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome, healed.
